intake.domain: systems and computer architecture for low-batch LLM inference on FPGA
intake.time: next systems/architecture submission cycle after July 2026
data: Gemma 3 1B F16 execution on an AMD Alveo U280
native llama.cpp/GGML traces: pp512 has 1,626 GGML calls expanded to 224,936 XRT launches; tg128 has 104,877 calls expanded to 202,530 XRT launches
GGML operator, tensor, artifact, and XRT traces from a strict-zero-fallback U280 backend
intake.compute: The user supplies one U280 prototype; the full falsification campaign is inferred as 80GB-class GPUs (A100/H100), up to 8 concurrent (one node), approximately 150 GPU-days over 5 months, plus a $10k inference/API budget.
intake.expertise: native C++ GGML/llama.cpp backend and XRT/FPGA systems engineering
intake.baseline: a native GGML/llama.cpp U280 backend with strict zero fallback, where every supported acceleration path must preserve native execution rather than silently redirect to a host implementation
intake.limitation: operator-granular native execution creates an extreme XRT launch count at low batch, yet any coarser delegation must preserve results, explicit failure, artifact identity, and zero fallback

bottleneck_statement: The structural failure is a contract-granularity mismatch for native, low-batch LLM execution: an FPGA wants a preplanned compute, memory, and synchronization interval, while the existing GGML caller exposes a long, stateful sequence of observable calls whose result, alias/ownership behavior, failure behavior, and artifact identity remain part of the program. Under that condition, current machinery either retains the original fine-grained dispatch sequence, so launch and synchronization costs are amplified, or specializes a fixed model, precision, and host-device split without determining whether a larger native interval is semantically legal and HBM-feasible; it therefore cannot produce a trustworthy delegation decision for a strict-zero-fallback backend. The closest FPGA Big-PE study integrates with Llama2 but only demonstrates 8-bit TinyStories prompt processing and leaves decode, KV cache, and larger Llama behavior unaddressed [openalex:W4416342314]; LlamaF relies on W8A8 TinyLlama, keeps transformer control and KV caches on the processing system, and specializes its matrix-vector path [openalex:W4405909140]; XtraMAC improves a mixed-precision MAC but reports no complete Llama-layer or KV-path integration [arxiv:2605.06052v1].

closest_adjacent.summary_and_residue: This work couples an open-source Llama2 framework to a U55 FPGA through XDMA/AXI and replaces scalar systolic cells with 4x4 Big PEs for 8-bit TinyStories prompt-stage matrix multiplication. It does not establish decode, KV-cache, larger-model, native-GGML, or strict observable-failure behavior, so its compute-density result does not close the end-to-end execution-contract gap. [residue is abstract-level: anchor fulltext unfetchable]

LlamaF uses W8A8 group-wise matrix-vector pipelines, asynchronous weight transfer, and a processing-system-resident transformer controller/KV cache for TinyLlama on ZCU102. Its acceleration contract is tied to quantized model-specific MVMs and explicitly leaves attention control and KV state outside the FPGA path, rather than covering an unmodified F16 GGML call stream.

XtraMAC unifies integer, floating-point, and mixed-precision MAC formats through shared mantissa products and runtime operand packing on U55c. It resolves a DSP-level format-sharing issue but provides no complete Llama-layer, KV-cache, host-runtime, or native-artifact execution contract.

what_phase_0_did_not_address: No retrieved frontier leaf establishes an observable end-to-end condition under which a heterogeneous native LLM call interval preserves its produced values, tensor/artifact identity, state effects, and explicit failure behavior while remaining valid across prefill and decode execution — stakes: strict-zero-fallback users can otherwise receive an unidentifiable or silently changed execution path, blocking trustworthy deployment and leaving systems results non-transferable across runtimes.

No retrieved frontier leaf establishes how low-batch execution can avoid launch-count-dominated latency when a long mixed GGML trace has dependencies, HBM capacity and access constraints, and runtime state that prevent treating arbitrary neighboring calls as one safe execution interval; the U280 pp512/tg128 traces are the primary instance — stakes: practitioners pay repeated XRT dispatch and synchronization costs that can erase accelerator benefit, while the field lacks a principled account of when coarse execution is actually legal rather than merely fast in a fixed benchmark.

No retrieved frontier paper tests whether the shared assumption that efficient LLM FPGA execution requires a compiler-owned, predeclared graph with fixed representation and host-device division is necessary rather than assumed — stakes: a negative answer would invalidate a common boundary in published accelerator conclusions, whereas leaving it unexamined can keep native-runtime deployment blocked despite apparently strong kernel or pipeline results.

method_lineage.line: LLM tensor execution from host-dispatched operators through compiler-owned static graph lowering to model-specific FPGA or persistent-engine implementations.

nodes.move: Executes each tensor operator through a host-visible runtime call and separate device work submission.
nodes.residual_problem: Repeated launch and whole-operator synchronization boundaries leave cross-operator latency and data movement exposed.

nodes.move: Moves a predeclared tensor graph into compiler-owned IR, fixed task connectivity, planned storage, and generated host/device code.
nodes.residual_problem: Generic static lowering still leaves LLM-specific compute density, mixed formats, and external-memory pressure to later specialized designs.

nodes.move: Lowers PyTorch/MLIR programs into hierarchical dataflow tasks with generated DMA, stream converters, FIFOs, design-space exploration, and host runtime code.
nodes.residual_problem: Its generated compiler/runtime owns the transformed PyTorch program, so it does not establish equivalence, artifact identity, or explicit no-fallback behavior for an unmodified GGML caller.

nodes.move: Jointly repairs dataflow violations, chooses FIFO or ping-pong communication, manages HBM transfers, and co-optimizes parallelism for C++ or PyTorch inputs.
nodes.residual_problem: It optimizes a compiler-transformed task graph but does not cover a native GGML call stream's observable ownership, failure, and zero-fallback requirements.

nodes.move: Compiles a PyTorch tensor program to a static SM-level task/event graph and runs it through an in-kernel worker/scheduler runtime to avoid operator-level launches.
nodes.residual_problem: The GPU/PyTorch mega-kernel assumes a compiler-produced static graph and does not establish an FPGA HBM path or a native GGML compatibility and failure contract.

nodes.move: Uses 4x4 matrix-multiplying processing elements to raise systolic compute density and integrates the array with an open-source Llama2 framework.
nodes.residual_problem: The reported path is 8-bit TinyStories prompt processing only; decode, KV state, larger models, and native-runtime semantics remain unclosed, with method-level residue unavailable after full-text top-up.

nodes.move: Specializes TinyLlama W8A8 matrix-vector computation and overlaps weight transfer with FPGA execution while retaining transformer control and KV cache on the processing system.
nodes.residual_problem: A model-specific quantized MVM contract leaves native F16 GGML execution, attention/KV ownership, and observable full-graph behavior outside its accelerated path.

nodes.move: Shares DSP-oriented integer mantissa products across integer, floating-point, and mixed-precision MAC modes with runtime operand packing.
nodes.residual_problem: A MAC-level improvement alone leaves region-level dependencies, HBM lifetimes, complete Llama execution, and the host-visible execution contract unresolved.

nodes.move: Keeps device workers resident across multiple logical tasks to remove repeated host launch boundaries.
nodes.residual_problem: Avoids relaunches but by itself does not establish an FPGA HBM implementation or native caller semantics.

nodes.move: Time-multiplexes operations over programmable coarse processing elements instead of fixing a fully spatial datapath per model.
nodes.residual_problem: Programmable execution flexibility alone does not prove compatibility with a native runtime's state, artifacts, or failure semantics.

nodes.move: Uses statically connected producer-consumer processes and FIFO communication to overlap stages.
nodes.residual_problem: A fixed stream topology does not decide whether a dynamic caller's interval is a legal region or preserve its observable fallback policy.

nodes.move: Overlaps transfer and compute through explicit tile residency and ping-pong buffers.
nodes.residual_problem: Memory-transfer overlap does not determine semantic region boundaries, identity, or explicit failure behavior.

method_lineage.notes: Retrieved nodes identify the current frontier, including user-reference full-text records; parametric nodes are awareness-only and are not prior-art claims. The shared ancestry-chain assumption is n1's compiler-owned, predeclared graph and fixed representation/host-device boundary. Collateral nodes record distinct older mechanism families so they are neither treated as gap sites nor mistaken for descendants.

domain_pattern_distribution.notes: Architectural_operator_substitution is most used; its closest papers improve a fixed compute or memory microarchitecture, but tend to leave native end-to-end runtime semantics and low-batch execution boundaries unestablished.
